cards.text: The prophet Ezekiel tells us that in the twenty-fifth year of exile, at the beginning of the year, on the tenth day of the month, fourteen years after Jerusalem was struck down, the hand of the LORD is upon him and He takes him somewhere. The twenty-fifth YEAR, friend. I spent years in a junk drawer, and by the end I was giving the dust names.

cards.question: In visions of God, where does the LORD take the exiled Ezekiel?

cards.text: He sets Ezekiel on a very high mountain, with something built on its southern slope. A VERY high mountain. Me, I have to hop, base and all, just to see over a mixing bowl.

cards.question: On the mountain's southern slope, Ezekiel sees a structure that resembles a ___.

cards.text: So He takes Ezekiel there, and a man is standing in the gateway. One look at this man and you know he is NOT your regular tour guide.

cards.question: The man standing in the gateway has an appearance like ___.
The bronze-looking man in the gateway is holding something in his hand. What is it?

answers.text: A linen cord and a measuring rod
A scroll and a writing reed
A trumpet and a burning lamp

cards.text: Then the man tells Ezekiel, “look with your eyes, hear with your ears,” and pay attention to everything he's about to show him, because that's why Ezekiel has been brought here. I half-listened to an oven timer once, friend, and I'm STILL scraping that batch off the pan.

cards.question: The man tells Ezekiel to keep everything he sees to himself.
The man tells Ezekiel to report everything he sees to the house of ___.

cards.text: So Ezekiel starts looking. The first thing he sees is a wall running all the way around the temple area.

cards.question: The man uses his measuring rod to measure the wall around the temple area.

cards.text: The man's measuring rod is six long cubits, and the wall comes out one rod thick and one rod high. This man measures EVERYTHING, and my measuring is a scoop, a squint and a prayer.

Then he measures the gates one by one, on the east, north and south, through the outer court and into the inner court. Every gate comes out fifty cubits long and twenty-five wide, all SIX of them, and I can't get two cookies to match.

In each of the inner gateways, by the portico, there's a chamber with a doorway, and it's there for a job with the offerings. That room's got one job, which is more than I could say for my old junk drawer.

cards.question: In the chamber by each inner gateway's portico, the ___ offering was to be washed.
Inside the portico of the gateway are two tables on each side. What were those tables for?

cards.text: Count them up: four tables inside the gateway and four outside by the north gate, eight in all. There are also four tables of dressed stone holding the tools for the sacrifices.
In the inner court there are two chambers: one beside the north gate facing south, and one beside the south gate facing north.

cards.question: The man says the two chambers in the inner court are for priests. What do the priests in the south-facing chamber keep charge of?
The man says the north-facing chamber is for the priests who keep charge of the altar.
Of the priests who keep charge of the altar, the man says these are the sons of ___, the only Levites who may approach the LORD to minister before Him.

cards.text: Next the man measures the inner court: square, a hundred cubits long and a hundred wide. My cookies are supposed to be ROUND, friend, and some days they can't even pull THAT off.

cards.question: In that square inner court, the ___ was in front of the temple.

cards.text: Then the man brings Ezekiel to the portico of the temple itself. It's twenty cubits wide and twelve cubits deep, with ten steps leading up to it.
There's a column by the side pillars, one on each side, and that's where we'll leave Ezekiel for now. Don't go anywhere, friend, because this tour is just getting started.
